g.text: "We're memory-constrained" doesn't mean the context window
When AI leaders say it, they mean HBM, in three different ways
1 · Bandwidth
decode re-reads the weights and the
KV cache from HBM for every token
more TB/s = more tokens per second
(H200 4.8 TB/s · Ironwood 7.4 TB/s)
see C3
2 · Capacity
HBM holds weights + KV cache
KV cache grows with every token of context
fixed GB per chip, so it's a trade:
longer context = fewer users at once
see C5
3 · Supply
only SK hynix, Samsung, Micron make HBM
Micron: "sold out for 2026"
1 bit of HBM costs ~3 bits of
ordinary DRAM in fab capacity
see C1c
the context window
is a consequence of
Said in public
Demis Hassabis (Google DeepMind): memory shortages are "constraining a lot of deployment".
Intel's Lip-Bu Tan calls HBM the biggest AI bottleneck.
One line to remember: the chips aren't short of maths. They're short of fast memory, and the whole world shares three suppliers of it.
